subject: maths
question: Aman goes to his office by car at the speed of 80 km/hr and reaches 10 minutes earlier. If he goes at the speed 30 km/hr, then he reaches 10 minutes late. What will be the speed of the car to reach on time?
solution:
**Given:**

Speed when Aman reaches 10 minutes earlier = 80 km/hr.

Speed when Aman reaches 10 minutes late = 30 km/hr.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Let the distance to the office be D km and the normal time to reach be T hours.

Time taken when speed is 80 km/hr = T - 10/60 hours

Time taken when speed is 30 km/hr = T + 10/60 hours

Using the formula Time = Distance / Speed:

D / 80 = T - 1/6

D / 30 = T + 1/6

We need to find the value of D and T first.

From the first equation: D = 80(T - 1/6)

From the second equation: D = 30(T + 1/6)

Equating both expressions for D:

80(T - 1/6) = 30(T + 1/6)

⇒ 80T - 80/6 = 30T + 30/6

⇒ 80T - 30T = 80/6 + 30/6

⇒ 50T = 110/6

⇒ T = 110/(6 × 50)

⇒ T = 11/30 hours

Now, substituting T back to find D:

D = 80(T - 1/6)

D = 80(11/30 - 1/6)

D = 80(11/30 - 5/30)

D = 80(6/30)

D = 80 × 1/5

D = 16 km

Now, to find the speed to reach on time:

Speed = Distance / Time

Speed = 16 / (11/30)

Speed = 16 × (30/11)

Speed = 480/11 km/hr

**The speed of the car to reach on time is 480/11 km/hr.**
